full_judgment: 19. Some of the gunny bags containing the ballot papers were found in torn condition and the learned appellate court found that the torn condition of the gunny bags was from the very beginning and it was not done by either parties and that the presumption of the mischief as alleged was not supported and established by the papers on record, although both the parties apprehended tampering with the election materials and both of them informed the Chief Election Commissioner and other authorities to keep the election papers in safe custody. However, there :is no specific case of tampering of any particular ballot paper or papers while those were in custody after the election was over. Mr. Chowdhury, however, submits that some ballot papers having double seals were wrongly excluded from the petitioner’s votes. The learned court below found those to have been rightly excluded. Mr. Chowdhury's contention that the deposition of DWs. were not considered and the deposition of P.W.4 was misinterpreted cannot be a ground for 'interference with the concurrent finding of facts arrived at by both the courts below based on evidence on record. Moreover the Presiding Officers were present at the time of recounting.
